statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 21%, inside the watch band and below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions describe a low-volatility trend-up session with the Nasdaq-100 printing at its session extreme. The narrow danger window is the 12:30-14:00Z August payrolls release on 4 September; outside that window the mapped state stays below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 grinds to a session high on Waller patience and an ISM Services beat, with August payrolls the next binary
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 29,464 (+1.10%), printing at the top of a 29,161-29,464 session range after opening near the low and extending through the morning. VIX is 14.83 at its daily low, the 2-year yield is 4.33% and the 10-year 4.75%, both lower after Fed Governor Waller signalled he is inclined to support holding the policy rate steady if disinflation continues. ISM Services beat at 55.4 against 54.3 consensus, with new orders at a three-and-a-half-year high, and initial jobless claims printed 206K. Software leads while semiconductors lag on mixed guidance; Nvidia gained after confirming a $13 billion acquisition of Hugging Face. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: gold is near $4,526, WTI is around $92.5 at six-week highs on renewed Middle East risk, and the dollar has fallen more than 2% against the yen to its weakest since late February. Observed one-way structure at the session extreme lifts Tail into the watch band, while low realised volatility, lagging semiconductors and a digested one-shot catalyst keep it below the block threshold. Stress stays elevated on the dollar dislocation, elevated oil and the payrolls binary in the forward window.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published state stayed green with Tail between 11% and 15%. Overnight and European hours were assessed as normal mode with Stress easing to the low 50s, before the U.S. morning shifted to mixed as the Waller comments and the ISM Services beat began repricing yields. The last two published hours already showed Tail ticking up from 13% to 14-15% as directional structure firmed.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail in the watch band while the session-high, one-way structure stands, with the Hammack speech at 19:00Z and the 20:00Z cash close as checkpoints. Risk is projected to fall back toward the low teens through the Asian session, then rebuild through European hours into the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, which is the mapped danger window. Tail is deliberately capped in the watch band across that release because event magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement price path.

One-way structure at the extreme lifts Tail into the watch band; low realised volatility caps the amplitude.
